result:
Done — typecheck and the full suite (7 tests, including the new ones) pass.

**What I changed:** I added a public JSON feed at `GET /api/posts` as a new route group in `routes/api.ts` (a `registerApiRoutes` registrar mirroring `routes/auth.ts`, called from `registerWebRoutes` in `routes/web.ts` so codegen and audit see it). The route is named `api.posts.index` and declares its contract inline: `query: ApiListPostsQuerySchema` (new in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` — `page` defaulting to 1 and an optional `author`, both coerced from strings and both rejecting `0`/non-numeric, which the router turns into a 422 JSON body before the controller runs) and `resource: { data: [PostResource] }`, the same response hint `posts.search` uses, so the regenerated `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` types `json()` as `{ data: Array<Data.Post> }`. The handler is `app/Http/Controllers/Api/PostController.ts`, which counts and fetches through separate builders rather than the ORM's `paginate()` helper — that helper skips eager loads, which would have dropped the `author` object the envelope promises — and returns `{ data, meta, links }` with posts newest-first, 10 per page, optionally filtered to one `authorId` (an author with no posts gets `200` with empty `data` and `total: 0`; a page past the end likewise returns an empty `data` for the page actually requested). I regenerated `.guren/routes.gen.ts` / `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` via `bun run codegen`, and added `tests/ApiPostController.test.ts` covering the route name in the manifest plus the four invalid-parameter cases; following the existing tests' convention it stays off the database, but I verified the listing, pagination, author filter, empty-author and 422 behaviour end-to-end with a throwaway test against the test database, then restored that database to its original seeded state.
